summary: GLOB performs case-sensitive Unix-style wildcard matching.
documentation: GLOB performs case-sensitive Unix-style wildcard matching. A bracket class such as [0-9] matches one character from a range, and the pattern describes the whole string unless wildcard characters extend it. It is not a regular expression or SQL LIKE pattern.
caution: GLOB uses * and ? rather than LIKE’s % and _. NULL input does not pass a WHERE predicate, and case sensitivity is intentional here.
scenarios: Filter documented import filenames by an ASCII code shape.
Select a local staging subset with a case-sensitive naming convention.
Find two-digit export references without relying on a regex extension.
title: Filter an exact filename shape
problem: Return ids whose name matches exactly INV- followed by two ASCII digits. Use GLOB 'INV-[0-9][0-9]' and order by id. Reject extra characters, lowercase prefixes and NULL.
hint: Bracket ranges match one character each; do not add * to the pattern.
goal: Use GLOB or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
